key_insight: The paper shows that variational quantum attacks on S-DES can be systematically improved by choosing the right combination of state preparation, ansatz, cost function, and optimizer.
engineering_relevance: It provides a benchmark framework for comparing NISQ-era quantum cryptanalysis designs, helping researchers identify which modular choices are most effective and practical.
method: Unified the attack pipeline into four modules: initial state, ansatz, cost function, and classical optimization.
Ran numerical simulations across representative design alternatives and their combinations.
Introduced standardized metrics to compare convergence, success probability, and effective time complexity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comprehensive numerical benchmarking that compares multiple modular configurations and evaluates them using convergence behavior, success probability, and effective time complexity.
watch_item: Results come from simulations on S-DES, so performance may not transfer directly to larger ciphers or real hardware noise conditions.
paper_title: A Modular Benchmark of Variational Quantum Attack Algorithms for S-DES
